author.continuation:
Session 11 of w02ca r6, block 1, packet w02ca-p02-003.3.

Gap 1 (Barwise p. 44, completeness for countable L_omega1omega theories with an infinitary rule) is written.
- The calculus is H_infinity. Its lines are sentences over L plus a countable set of parameters. It has infinitary tautologies, equality and quantifier axioms for closed terms, modus ponens, parameter generalization, and R3, a conjunction rule with countably many premises.
- Proved (assuming AC): soundness; every theorem uses countably many premises; syntactic negation normal form; model existence with function symbols (term Hintikka sets); and the main result: for any language and any countable T, T |-_infinity phi iff T |= phi.
- Worked example: a derivation that uses R3.
- Failure case: an uncountable theory with no model that proves no contradiction.
- Barwise names no rule, so this is the handbook's calculus. It is not Karp's calculus, which stays cited in thm:p02-karp-completeness. Karp 1964 is not held. The open-access Lopez-Escobar 1965 copy (Fund. Math. 57) returned HTTP 403 and was not read.

Gap 2 (Barwise p. 37) is written in the w02-p02-005 host body and annex.
- System H-circ: the axioms of H, modus ponens, and the rules 4.11(iii),(iv) in place of generalization. Proviso: v not free in psi; y = v, or y not free in phi(v) and substitutable.
- Proved: soundness at every assignment; clause (v) derived without generalization, via D = not exists y not phi(y) -> forall y phi(y) obtained by (iv) with a fresh variable; completeness for sentences, so H-circ and H prove the same sentences.
- Also written: an example and a warning showing why both provisos are needed.
- Open: completeness under the narrower 4.11 proviso (y not occurring in phi(v)). It needs an alphabetic-variant lemma that is not written; this is recorded in warning def:p02-w02c-p02-003-h-circ-proviso and in the research note's Missing work item 11.
